resources.string: Uses the smaller supported buffer in Low latency mode. More sensitive to processing stalls; turn this off first if audio breaks up. The displayed target fill is not total playback latency.
Uses root on supported system builds to reduce internal waiting. Low latency only. Standard capture is kept if unavailable; turn off if audio breaks up under load.
Use the dedicated capture path in Low latency mode. Requires root. Turn off to use standard capture. Unsupported devices use standard capture automatically.

Selected app shares the app chosen in media output. Whole device shares playback and notification sounds across apps. Microphone and call audio are excluded. Changing modes reconnects at 0% volume.

Preserve captured 44.1 kHz / 16-bit stereo without discarding samples. Uses a 150 ms reserve and 1500 ms receiver target for stable listening. Low latency uses the same audio precision. This does not turn the source into high-resolution audio.
Reserve %1$d ms · Capture %2$.1f ms · Presentation target %3$d ms\nChanging profiles reconnects at 0%% volume.

ON compresses audio without changing samples. OFF restores uncompressed ALAC frames. Independent of the audio profile. Data savings depend on the sound; compression may not reduce delay. Changes reconnect at 0% volume.
Fine-tune delay and buffering. Applying values switches both audio profiles off and retains the compression choice.

2 ms capture blocks and a 50 ms receiver target. Shorter targets may connect without audible playback. This is not measured end-to-end delay. Adaptive buffering starts near 8 ms; turn it off for a 0 ms reserve. Turn this mode off if dropouts increase. Applying Latency and buffers switches to custom settings. Changes reconnect at 0% volume.
Reserve auto 8–48 ms · Capture %1$.1f ms · Presentation target %2$d ms\nChanging profiles reconnects at 0%% volume.

Starts near 8 ms and increases only as needed after input shortages, up to 48 ms. Reduces again during sustained silence, trimming only excess zero samples. Audible samples are retained. Each new connection starts small. OFF uses a 0 ms reserve. Changes reconnect at 0% volume.

Smaller values can reduce delay but increase dropouts. Actual latency also depends on HomePod and the network. Targets below 50 ms are experimental and may produce no sound on HomePod even when connected. Applying settings reconnects at 0% volume.

This preset fixes these values. Switch to custom settings to edit supported values. Dedicated capture is only active in Low latency mode. Independent receiver timing is configured separately.

In dedicated Low latency mode, group about 2 ms of audio per packet instead of 8 ms. Audio remains lossless. This increases packet count and is unverified with HomePod. Turn off if playback fails. Standard capture and high quality keep 8 ms packets. Changes reconnect at 0% volume.
Uses a 1.09 ms phone mixer period on compatible rooted Galaxy devices. Requires Low latency and Dedicated capture. Incompatible routes use fallback capture. This does not set the HomePod delay.
Dedicated capture active · 1.09 ms phone mixer
Choose one profile. Low latency uses the dedicated phone path; High quality prioritizes playback stability. All numeric overrides are grouped under Fully manual.
Specify each configurable value here. Applying switches to Fully manual and reconnects once. Presets do not override manual numbers, and automatic buffer adjustment is disabled in manual mode.
1.09–21.04 ms. Rounded to the closest supported period.
1.09–18.14 ms (48–800 frames). Rounded to a whole frame. Small reserves with long mixer periods may interrupt audio.
The earlier 1.18–10.50 ms values were measured average queued audio. They vary with playback and load; the reserve target is a separate setting.
Dedicated read unit: 0.50 ms (22 frames, fixed).
88 (2.00 ms) or 352 (7.98 ms). Standard/fallback capture uses 352. HomePod compatibility with 88 is unverified.
Receiver timing is independent of phone buffering. All three values: 10–2000 ms.
